summary: Request timeouts on long-context prompts / large max_tokens settings
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated request timeouts when sending long-context prompts (approx 250k tokens) or very large max_tokens (>=50k) values. Failures manifest as 504/timeout on the hosted API after ~60s. Impact: Tenant-facing production errors causing degraded user-facing features for Acme Financial (chat-history retrieval and summarization flows). Environment: prod, us-east region, customer on enterprise plan with dedicated routing. Steps to reproduce:
1) Use API endpoint /v1/generate with model=redwood-13b-v2.
2) Attach prompt consisting of large conversation history (~200-300k tokens).
3) Set max_tokens to 50k and streaming=false.
4) Observe request hanging and then returning 504 after ~60s.
Logs/response: Customer provided request_id: rq_20260220_acme_07. Server-side logs show request queued for batching, then dropped after rpc timeout. Recent changes: Autoscaler config adjusted 2026-02-19 to reduce short-lived scale-ups; kernel selection change merged 2026-02-18 (PR #1284) that changed loop preemption threshold. Hypothesis: Large token count + large max_tokens is triggering excessive KV cache allocation and prolonged compilation/kernel selection, causing enqueue/backpressure and eventual API gateway timeout. Alternative hypothesis: Autoscaler policy now delays spot/scale-up for long-running requests, increasing queue wait time. Next steps: 1) Reproduce in staging with customer's payload and instrumentation enabled. 2) Temporarily advise customer to lower max_tokens and enable streaming to reduce single-request memory. 3) SRE to add detailed enqueue/queue-time metrics and increase rpc timeout for dedicated tenants as emergency mitigation. 4) If reproduced, roll back PR #1284 candidate or patch kernel selection path to avoid long blocking operations.

2026-02-20 13:30 UTC - Elena Martinez (Serving Runtime): Able to reproduce a timeout in staging when simulating 220k token context + max_tokens 50k. Observed heavy KV allocation and a compilation stall on kernel selection. Adding instrumentation for allocation size and kernel-selection duration.

2026-02-21 09:10 UTC - Marcus Lee (SRE): Temporarily increased RPC gateway timeout for enterprise dedicated routing to 120s for Acme Financial to mitigate immediate customer impact. Notified billing/CS.

2026-02-22 15:45 UTC - Elena Martinez (Serving Runtime): Patch candidate ready to short-circuit kernel selection for large context cases (PR #1290). Requesting approval for canary in us-east staging first.

investigation_notes: Reproduction: Confirmed in staging using customer's payload. Timeout correlated with queue wait time and backend compilation stalls.
Metrics: Queue_time spiked to 45-55s for affected requests. Backend processing time under 10s once kernel selection completed.
Correlation: Change window around 2026-02-18 where kernel selection preemption threshold was modified (PR #1284).
Memory: KV cache allocation peaked and caused GC-like stalls in the runtime when handling very large contexts.
Autoscaler behavior: Short-lived scale-ups suppressed by new autoscaler policy, contributing ~10-15s additional queue time under burst.
Mitigation tested: Streaming + lower max_tokens prevented queue buildup in customer tests. Increasing RPC timeout reduced immediate customer errors but doesn't fix root cause.
next_steps: Approve and deploy serving-runtime short-circuit patch (PR #1290) to canary in us-east staging.
Add queue_time and kernel_selection_time dashboards and alert (SRE/Observability).
Evaluate autoscaler policy tuning for long-running large-context requests and consider tenant-aware fast-paths.
Follow up with customer with ETA and recommended temporary config (streaming=true, max_tokens<=10k, split long-contexts).
resolution: Workaround provided: customer enabled streaming and reduced max_tokens to 10k; SRE increased RPC timeout for enterprise routing as temporary mitigation. Patch PR #1290 prepared for canary. Pending deployment and verification.
